cycle.note: Minnesota CPE years run July 1 – June 30 and are reported by December 31. Each year needs 20 hours; the rolling three CPE years need 120, with 60 technical, 8 ethics and 24 group or blended.

requirements.label: Three-year total
requirements.note: The three CPE years ending June 30 must reach 120 hours.

requirements.label: Minimum each year
requirements.note: At least 20 hours every CPE year (July 1 – June 30), reported by December 31.

requirements.label: Technical
requirements.note: At least 60 of the 120 from technical subjects (NASBA technical fields of study, including Regulatory Ethics).

requirements.label: Group or blended learning
requirements.note: At least 24 of the 120 from group (live or online live) or blended programs. We use each course's delivery format.

requirements.label: Ethics
requirements.note: 8 hours of regulatory or behavioral ethics in the rolling three CPE years.

newLicensee.note: No CPE is due for the CPE year you were licensed in; your first CPE year starts the next July 1.

licenseDateHint: Minnesota licenses renew every year on December 31. CPE years run July 1 – June 30 regardless.
issueDateHint: If you were licensed this CPE year (since July 1), no CPE is due until the next July 1.
limitsNotTracked: At least 72 of the 120 from approved CPE sponsors (NASBA Registry sponsors, peer-reviewed firms, universities, professional organizations).
Instruction: max 60 hours; published materials: max 60 hours.
The same self-study course can't be repeated for credit within one CPE year.
Carryback: hours after June 30 can count for the prior CPE year with late fees, but only once.
toVerify: New licensees: the three-year totals (120, 60 technical, 24 group, 8 ethics) are treated as not due until three full CPE years after licensure; each year's 20 still applies.
Technical = NASBA's technical fields of study, with Regulatory Ethics technical and Behavioral Ethics non-technical.
